after: The Interference Sign Error in Conventional Routing
title: Conceptual view. Interference is both fuel and risk.
caption: HOPE's routing weight rewards transmitter-side interference because it shortens harvesting time, while penalizing receiver-side interference because it raises outage pressure. The chosen path is the one that balances those two effects, not merely the shortest or quietest path.

title: Fig. 2. Route selection under interference-powered harvesting.
caption: A 30-node, 20-interferer network snapshot comparing HOPE, MER, and shortest-path routes. HOPE deliberately exploits the spatial distribution of interferers instead of simply avoiding them.

after: Analysis: Why Minimum-Energy Routing Loses Here
title: Fig. 3. Latency versus number of interferers.
caption: HOPE remains comparatively stable as interferer density rises, while MER latency increases because it treats interference primarily as a reliability burden rather than an energy source.

title: Fig. 4. Latency versus number of system nodes.
